sentences.text: The generic name Cedrorestes means "mountain cedar dweller," derived from the formation where it was found.
The type specimen DMNH 47994 is a partial skeleton containing rib fragments, a sacrum, ilia, a thighbone, a metatarsal, and ossified tendon fragments.
Cedrorestes is distinguished by a combination of a tall ilium like Iguanodon and a large lateral bony process near the hip joint typical of hadrosaurids.
The species name crichtoni honors author Michael Crichton, who wrote Jurassic Park and The Lost World.
Cedrorestes was estimated to be about 6 meters long and weigh 1500 kilograms.
Cedrorestes is known from an incomplete skeleton found in the Valanginian-age Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation.
The remains of Cedrorestes were recovered in 2001 from the top of the Yellow Cat Member in east-central Utah.
The hip structure suggests hadrosaurid-like leg muscles, but the functional differences in movement compared to iguanodontians remain unclear.
Cedrorestes lived alongside other dinosaurs including the theropod Utahraptor, the sauropod Cedarosaurus, and the armored dinosaur Gastonia.
The genus was originally classified in Hadrosauridae as the earliest known member of that family.
Researchers placed the genus within Hadrosauridae as a basal member.
Cedrorestes lived during the Early Cretaceous period in Utah.
Cedrorestes lived during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 130 to 125 million years ago, in what is now North America.
Fossil evidence places Cedrorestes in the Valanginian stage between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago.
It is debated whether Cedrorestes represents a basal hadrosaurid or a derived non-hadrosaurid iguanodontian.
While hip structures suggest hadrosaurid-like muscles, the specific differences in movement compared to iguanodontians are not yet clear.
